doc.title: "Papa Jack" Laine, Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine and Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1959-02-27

title: Emile Christian's trombone playing today
summary: Wiggs says Emile Christian plays better than ever with false teeth, recorded on his Mardi Gras records, and Blanche notes he lives next door.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: You know, you ought to hear Emile Christian now. Oh, Emile plays a good trombone. They tell me. I don't know. I mean to tell you, he is terrific now. Is he?
I thought he couldn't play no more.
He's ten times better than he ever was. I spoke to him Monday.
He got his teeth out.

They won't hire him because he's an old man, you see? But I played with him. You know that, uh, you know that time you, uh... I see. You know that time I said that Brunus boy hired us for across the river? Yeah. I got Emile. I've been recording with Emile, too.
Yeah. Emile is, I tell you, he's... Emile is about 64 years old.
He's older than that, isn't he?
No. Mm-mm. He's one year older than my son. They work together at the Postal Telegraph and everything else.
Yeah. I spoke to him Monday.
Yeah. Yeah, I spoke to him Monday, yeah. Emile Christian. They're living right next to us. He was a good friend, I'll tell you. Oh, I tell you.
You should have heard him that day we played across the river, Emile.
Emile. But I tell you, he really aged, though, didn't he? That's the total.

Yeah, he looks old, but he played that trombone like a 25-year-old boy that day. He was a good trombone player, though, Hank. His brother was a good one, too, but... I'm telling you, he played some licks that would have been hard to play on trumpet. Yeah. And I mean, he just executed them perfectly. They weren't any corny licks. They were good. Clear. Every note in them were... Every note was well selected. You know, clever. Clear, yeah. Oh, I mean...
Well, he stopped playing on the kind of his teeth. No. No?
He got some false teeth specially made for that. Oh, he's got them. And I'm telling you, he plays better on those false teeth than he ever played in his life.
Oh, no kidding. I thought you couldn't play with false teeth.
He's got two sets of them. One for eating and one for playing. Oh, I never thought that...
I broke some money in the baker shop.
Yeah?
When I come from the doctor.

Yeah? I guess he's disgusted because, you know, he's old and they won't hire him. Oh. You see? Yeah. And he's wonderful. Ain't that something? He's wonderful. I got him on those, you know, those Mardi Gras records I made, the If Ever I Cease to Love, and King Zulu Parade, and those records. Yeah. And oh, he's just wonderful. Let me tell you a little story, Johnny. He was good.
I know he was.
